articles.title: Celtic fans throw tennis balls at club owner Dermot Desmond during golf tournament
articles.summary: Fans staged protest during pro-am tournament. Desmond escorted off St Andrews course by security. Celtic’s principal shareholder Dermot Desmond had tennis balls thrown towards him during his visit to the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament at St Andrews in a protest from fans.
body: The 76-year-old – who has been criticised by supporters for an apparent lack of progress on the pitch – was taking part in the pro-am event on Saturday when the disruption happened on the green of the 15th hole.
Tennis balls with pictures of Desmond’s face crossed out were thrown on to the green, with Desmond then escorted off the course by security.
The Celtic Fans Collective later released a statement on X, which included video and pictures of the protest, calling for change at the top of the club.

“Dermot Desmond has essentially been allowed to run Celtic Football Club whilst using his wealth to hide from supporters and accountability,” the statement said. “Fans took the chance today to send a message that this arrangement cannot continue.”

articles.title: Kane and Saka double up as England school Croatia in historic Nations League rout
articles.summary: It had all the edge of a pop concert in the stands but England looked ready to steal candy from a baby. The 6,200 Croatian under-14s allowed inside Stadion HNK Rijeka were invited free of charge and this was a priceless footballing experience.
body: Perhaps the ticket should have come with an adult age rating. This was grisly viewing for the locals but Thomas Tuchel delighted in England’s most complete performance since surging to a 4-2 win over Croatia at the World Cup. Kane marked his 124th cap with his 88th and 89th international strikes and had plenty of help. Three assists and a goal decorated a scintillating display from Bellingham and Tuchel found satisfaction in the other members of his ruthless front four getting on the scoresheet.

Everything clicked. England could have had double figures against opponents ranked 12th in the world but they settled for seven. Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka were in lightning, goalscoring form on the flanks and another story was an exceptional full debut from Alex Scott. The 22-year-old proved that he belongs, impressing with his tenacity and quality on and off the ball, and made it hard to shake off the sense that Tuchel missed a trick by not taking him to the World Cup.

articles.title: Wu thrashes Trump to set up Yuan final in Shenzhen
articles.summary: Chinese world champion Wu Yize wins six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 at the Shenzhen Open and set up a final against countryman Yuan Sijun.
body: Reigning world champion Wu Yize won six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 in the Shenzhen Open semi-finals.

Wu, who will leapfrog Trump in the rankings and move second in the world after the final, bounced back in dramatic fashion after losing the opening frame to set up an all-Chinese final against Yuan Sijun at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.
Yuan, 26, endured a much more difficult route to his maiden ranking final, battling through 6-5 against Englishman Jimmy Robertson.
World number two Trump, who won the Shanghai Masters in August, had gone into the Shenzhen semi-final in fine form after beating Mark Selby 5-0 in the last eight.

articles.title: Why Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy was actually a steal, and not an overpay
articles.summary: McCarthy was actually a steal, and not an overpay originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The New York Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the 2026 season after Week 2 and knew they needed to go out and add at least one quarterback.
body: Their decision was to acquire J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings, an intriguing pickup of a quarterback who has become a complete bust for the Vikings. They sent a 2027 fifth-round pick to land the Vikings' former first-round QB.

That price was considered an overpay by some in the NFL, according to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic. But Jones also outlined a very important point as to why this might be a steal, and not an overpay.

"Sources I spoke to around the league ahead of the trade anticipated McCarthy would be dealt for a sixth-round pick, so a fifth was better than expected for new Vikings GM Nolan Teasley," Jones writes.
That isn't a massive difference in trade value for McCarthy, but if teams expected him to go for a sixth-rounder, and the Giants sent a fifth, then they did overpay, even if only a little bit.

articles.title: Group has 'exploded' after Wales win - Bellamy
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy says Wales' win over Norway has "thrown a hand grenade" into their Nations League group as they go in search of another victory against Denmark in Cardiff on Sunday.
body: Wales remain bottom of Group A4 despite Thursday's morale-boosting triumph over Norway, though they are level on points with the World Cup quarter-finalists and Denmark at the halfway point in the campaign.
They would take a big step towards avoiding a last-place finish by beating Denmark on Sunday (19:45 BST) and receive a significant boost to their European Championship qualification hopes.
If Wales end their Nations League campaign in third place or higher, they will be a top seed in December's draw for Euro 2028 qualifying.
Bellamy says Portugal will win the group "unless a disaster happens" - but feels the race for the places is wide open after his side shocked Norway.

articles.title: India win Asian Games - but denied ODI sweep over West Indies by superb Hope
articles.summary: India beat Pakistan in T20 cricket to secure back-to-back gold medals at the Asian Games - but their ODI side were unable to complete a 3-0 sweep of West Indies on the same day after Shai Hope's 162 not out led the tourists to their record chase of 352.
body: In the Asian Games final in Japan, India smoked 211-6 from their 20 overs, underpinned by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 balls, Tilak Varma's 51 not out from 22 and Shivam Dube's 27 off 15.
Pakistan plummeted to 39-3 in reply and despite Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51 balls, they could muster only 192-6 and lost by 19 runs.
The victory was India's seventh in a row over Pakistan in T20Is and their 14th in the 18 matches between the teams in the format.

In New Chandigarh, however, India saw their total of 351-7 eclipsed by West Indies with 10 balls to spare as visiting captain Hope struck his 21st ODI hundred and second in as many matches to secure a five-wicket win after defeats in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati.

articles.title: Germany U19 end international break with unbeaten record after Czechia draw
articles.summary: Germany U19 drew 1-1 with Czechia in their third and last friendly in Spain ahead of next month’s qualification games for the European championship. Hanno Balistch’s side beat Finland in the middle of stalemates with Ukraine and Czechia.
body: After a goalless draw with the side coached by former Arsenal defender Oleh Luzhnyi, Noah Ringbeck’s brace helped Germany to a 2-1 victory over Finland on Wednesday.

Alexander Staff, who scored 21 goals at the U16 and U17 level, got his first goal for the U19 with a first-half penalty-kick against Czechia on Saturday. Idris Hopi scored the equalizing goal after the break for the hosts of the 2027 U19 Euros.

Germany will face Lithuania, Portugal and Sweden as the second round of the U19 Euros qualification starts in November. Balitsch’s side lost to record winners Spain in the most recent final of the annual competition.
That result already confirmed their place for the 50th anniversary of the U20 World Cup that will be co-hosted by Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

articles.title: Caballo De Mar upsets Scandinavia in Cadran clash
articles.summary: Caballo De Mar brought an end to Scandinavia’s eight-race winning run when repeating his win in the Qatar Prix du Cadran from 12 months ago in a thrilling finish at ParisLongchamp.
body: After surviving a lengthy stewards' enquiry, Caballo De Mar retained his Prix du Cadran crown, defeating red-hot favourite Scandinavia in a thrilling renewal of the Group 1 staying contest at ParisLongchamp.
George Scott's stayer was delivered by Oisin Murphy at the furlong marker to grab the lead from Scandinavia and the fading pacesetter Queenstown.
As the pair locked horns through the final furlong, Scandinavia regained the lead only for Caballo De Mar to fight back in the shadow of the post to get up by a neck.
Connections had to sweat through a stewards' inquiry after an objection by Ryan Moore, whose mount Scandinavia, the 1-6 favourite, appeared to receive a bump from the 9-2 winner close to the finish.
